page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-24-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 186.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.75 GB of RAM per core, and includes 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across four bundled drives. The processor runs at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and features a 504 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-threaded performance, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 36.68 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.42 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested instances. The Geekbench single-core score of 2321.0 also ranks in the top 10%, while the multi-core score of 16159.0 falls within the top 25%. For machine learning workloads, the instance demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds of 2400.47 tokens/sec and top-tier text generation speeds of 394.37 tokens/sec using a small 135M parameter LLM. However, performance scales down to average levels for larger workloads, with medium 7B model prompt processing executing at 151.39 tokens/sec and text generation at 20.25 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-24-lssd balances high memory density and local NVMe storage without the added expense of a dedicated GPU. The inclusion of 1.3 TB of local SSD storage makes it suitable for IOPS-heavy applications. This hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive and storage-reliant workloads, such as database operations, memory-cached web serving, and localized data processing. The presence of AMX instructions also supports CPU-based machine learning inference for smaller models, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for larger deep learning tasks.
